Illustration: a sunny winter day in Lapland. On the left is a log lean-to shelter with snow on its roof. In front of the shelter a campfire burns in a ring of stones, and above it a black, sooty pot full of snow hangs from a tripod. Steam rises from the pot. Beside the campfire is a bucket of snow. In the background are snowy fells and spruces.
Käsitekartta. Ylhäällä solmu energia säi: Concept map. At the top is the node energy is conserved: in an isolated system the quantity of heat released equals the quantity received. Four branches lead down from it. Heating: Q = c m ΔT when the state does not change, and the kelvin temperature T = θ + 273.15. Change of state: melting Q = s m and vaporisation Q = r m at constant temperature. Thermal expansion: length ΔL = α L0 ΔT and volume ΔV = γ V0 ΔT. Heat transfer: conduction, convection and radiation, and the power conducted through a wall P = U A ΔT.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: kilogramman lumen: Graph to scale: the temperature T of a kilogram of snow in degrees Celsius as a function of the energy transferred Q in kilojoules. The snow warms from −10 degrees to 0 degrees when 21 kJ of energy has been transferred. Then the temperature stays at 0 degrees until 355 kJ of energy has been transferred: melting takes Q = s m = 334 kJ. The meltwater warms to 100 degrees when 774 kJ of energy has been transferred: this takes Q = c m ΔT = 419 kJ. After that the water boils at 100 degrees, and the graph continues as a horizontal arrow, because vaporisation Q = r m would still need 2260 kJ.
Kuvaaja: höyrystyneen veden massa Δm vii: Graph: the mass Δm of water vaporised in five minutes as a function of the power P of the immersion heater. Five black points at powers of 200–1000 W. A rising straight line is fitted to the points and extended as a dashed line to the horizontal axis and up to the power 1100 W. The line passes through the points (100 W; 4 g) and (1100 W; 137 g); these two points of the line are circled, and the slope, about 0.133 g/W, is read from them. The line crosses the horizontal axis at a power of about 70 W. The line does not pass through the origin.
